domain: Diablo 2 Resurrected — edge-case roll-dependent unique items (mature ladder economy). Uniques whose value comes almost entirely from the variable roll, socket count, or ethereal state, not the item name.

items.name: Verdungo's Hearty Cord
items.quality: Perfect = 15% Damage Reduced / +40 Vitality (top form also 13 replenish / 140 ED)
items.rarityTier: Common drop, genuinely rare perfect roll
items.priceSignal: Real demand exists at the top of the roll: a perfect 15%DR/40vit trades roughly Ist–Vex non-ladder, Vex–Lo ladder per d2jsp price-check threads; one concrete 15DR/32vit/140ED copy went for ~250 FG. Peaked near an Ohm in 2022. A 10%DR/30vit copy is near-vendor and gets waved off — that spread IS the item.
items.collectorCase: The name is common but the double-perfect is the museum piece. Value lives entirely in two rolls; the belt with the lowest DR and lowest vit is trash while the 15/40 is a chase belt. A seasoned player who thinks 'I have a Verdungo, I'm set' is holding a different item than the collector's 15/40.
items.whyValuable: Only belt in the game that pairs a % damage-reduction mod with the largest vitality/life boost of any belt — it is the survivability cap for melee and hardcore. The % DR is a rare belt affix and stacks toward DR breakpoints.
items.teachingPoint: DR% is flat mitigation: going 10%→15% is 50% more damage reduction from the item, not a 5% nudge. Traders quote rolled/max shorthand — '15/40' means 15-of-15 DR, 40-of-40 vit; a fuller quote is '15/40/13/140' (DR / vit / replenish / ED).
items.veteranBlindspot: Veterans treat 'a Verdungo' as a solved slot and under-price the roll gap. The replenish and ED numbers are noise; only DR% and vit move the price, and most dropped copies are mediocre on at least one.
factClaims: Verdungo's Hearty Cord is a unique Mithril Coil (elite belt).
Damage Reduced by 10-15% is variable; perfect is 15%.
+30-40 to Vitality is variable; perfect is 40.
Replenish Life +10-13 is variable.
+90-140% Enhanced Defense is variable.
It also carries Increase Maximum Stamina by 30-40%.
The two stats traders price on are Damage Reduced % and Vitality.

items.name: Griffon's Eye
items.category: Circlet/Diadem (elite unique) — roll-dependent, unequal stat weighting
items.quality: Perfect = -20% Enemy Lightning Resist / +15% Lightning Skill Damage
items.rarityTier: Rare drop; perfect two-stat roll scarce
items.priceSignal: Strong, durable demand — a -20/high copy is quoted around Sur to multiple Ohm on diablo2.io/d2jsp; a -20/12 example was listed at Sur+. The important nuance: traders pay for the -Lightning Resist half and shrug at the +Lightning Skill Damage half (there is a diablo2.io thread literally titled 'Why -LR way more important than +LD').
items.collectorCase: Two variable stats that markets weight very differently. A -20/10 and a -15/15 look similar to a novice but the -20/10 is worth far more, because -Enemy Lightning Resist punches through Hell immunities/resistances multiplicatively. The collector piece is -20 res first, then +15 dmg on top.
items.whyValuable: Best-in-slot helm for lightning Sorc, Javazon, and any lightning build: the only helm granting -% enemy lightning resistance plus +% lightning skill damage, on top of +1 skills and 25% FCR.
items.teachingPoint: When a unique has two variable stats, they are rarely priced equally. Here the single stat that matters is -Enemy Lightning Resistance; one point (-19 vs -20) can move it a tier because enemy resist reduction is a multiplier against Hell targets.
items.veteranBlindspot: Even strong players quote Griffon's as one number. The market doesn't — a -15/15 is a budget piece and a -20/12 is the chase. The +Lightning Skill Damage roll is close to a tiebreaker, not the value.
factClaims: Griffon's Eye is a unique Diadem, required level 76.
+1 to All Skills and +25% Faster Cast Rate are fixed.
-15 to -20% to Enemy Lightning Resistance is variable; perfect is -20.
+10 to 15% to Lightning Skill Damage is variable; perfect is +15.
+100-200 Defense is variable.
Community consensus prices the -Enemy Lightning Resistance roll above the +Lightning Skill Damage roll.

items.name: Death's Fathom
items.category: Sorceress orb (elite unique) — single-stat multiplier roll
items.quality: Perfect = +30% Cold Skill Damage (top form 30/40/40 with both resists maxed)
items.priceSignal: Heavily demanded by cold Sorcs; a 30% copy sits at the top of the price-check charts (diablo2.io item #744) and is stocked as the premium tier by every item shop, distinctly above 20-24% and 25-29% brackets that vendors literally sort into separate SKUs. A 15-20% roll is a budget orb.
items.collectorCase: The name is one item; the roll makes two economies. +% Cold Skill Damage is its own damage multiplier layered on the build, so a 15% and a 30% are not '15% apart' — the 30% is the museum orb and the reason shops bin Fathoms by 5% roll bands.
items.whyValuable: The only Sorceress weapon that grants +% Cold Skill Damage, and it stacks with everything else a Blizzard/Orb sorc runs. Also +3 sorc skills and 20 FCR baseline.
items.teachingPoint: A '+% skill damage' roll is a direct multiplier, which is why 1% is worth real money and vendors price Fathoms in 5% tiers. Bonus edge case: because casting never drains durability, an ethereal Death's Fathom never breaks for a caster — a pure collector flex with a sliver of extra defense and zero downside.
items.veteranBlindspot: Vets know Fathom is BiS but often accept any Fathom; the market treats the 30% as a different item, and the ethereal-caster copy is a connoisseur piece most players never think to chase.
factClaims: Death's Fathom is a unique Dimensional Shard (elite Sorceress orb), required level 73.
+3 to Sorceress Skill Levels and +20% Faster Cast Rate are fixed.
+15-30% to Cold Skill Damage is variable and is the value stat; perfect is 30%.
Lightning Resist +25-40% and Fire Resist +25-40% are variable.
It is the only Sorceress weapon granting +% Cold Skill Damage.
Because spellcasting does not consume durability, an ethereal Death's Fathom does not break for a caster.

items.name: Nightwing's Veil
items.quality: Perfect = +15% Cold Skill Damage / +120% ED / +20 dex / +9 cold absorb
items.valueTierGuess: B (A for a perfect on a cold caster)
items.rarityTier: Rare drop; perfect cold-damage roll scarce
items.priceSignal: Solid demand from cold Sorcs and cold-based casters; diablo2.io tracks it (item #865) and shops split inventory into '15% Cold Dmg' premium vs '10-14% Cold Dmg' budget SKUs, which is the tell that the roll drives price. A near-perfect real copy (117ED/14 cold dmg/20 dex/8 absorb) was posted as a trade highlight.
items.collectorCase: It is the cold-damage counterpart to Griffon's, but veterans buy it for +2 skills and cold absorb and never read the cold-damage line. The perfect 15% is a hidden-value helm: same slot, meaningfully more damage, and the roll is what separates a 4-Ist helm from a chase piece.
items.whyValuable: Rare stacking of +2 all skills, +% cold skill damage, dexterity, and cold absorb on one helm — the best non-circlet caster damage helm for cold builds, and a top merc helm for the ED/absorb.
items.teachingPoint: The value stat (Cold Skill Damage) is buried under flashier fixed stats (+2 skills). Same lesson as Fathom — it's a multiplier, so 8%→15% is a real damage jump, but here even seasoned players skip reading it.
items.veteranBlindspot: Most players evaluate Nightwing's on +2/absorb and treat the cold-damage roll as flavor. It's the opposite — that roll is the price driver on a cold caster.
factClaims: Nightwing's Veil is a unique Spired Helm (elite), required level 67.
+90-120% Enhanced Defense is variable.
+2 to All Skills is fixed.
+8-15% to Cold Skill Damage is variable and is the value stat; perfect is 15%.
+10-20 to Dexterity is variable.
+5-9 Cold Absorb is variable.
It carries Half Freeze Duration.

items.name: Wisp Projector
items.category: Ring (elite unique) — absorb roll, extreme drop rarity
items.rarityTier: Extremely rare — regarded as the hardest unique ring to drop
items.priceSignal: Real, roll-sensitive demand: diablo2.io lists it as the rarest unique ring, and a 20% absorb copy is priced well above a 10% one. Not a mass-market item — value comes from scarcity plus the top absorb roll; low-absorb copies still sell on rarity alone but at a fraction.
items.collectorCase: Genuinely a museum ring: the rarest unique ring in the game, and its only reason to exist — % lightning absorb — is a variable 10-20 roll. A 20% copy is a two-way collector piece (rarity + roll). Many veterans have never held one.
items.whyValuable: Lightning absorb turns lightning damage into healing/mitigation; paired with high resist it makes a character nearly immune to lightning (Uber Meph, Burning Souls, Gloams). Also carries MF and Oak Sage/other charges.
items.teachingPoint: Socket count doesn't apply to rings — here the roll and the drop rarity together set price. It's the cleanest case where the entire point of an item is one variable number, and the number ranges 2x (10→20).
items.veteranBlindspot: Dismissed as a niche 'anti-Gloam' toy, but a perfect 20% is both a functional lightning-immunity enabler and a rarity trophy — the kind of thing veterans forget can be worth chasing.
factClaims: Wisp Projector is a unique Ring, required level 76.
It is widely regarded as the rarest unique ring to obtain.
Lightning Absorb 10-20% is variable and is the value stat; perfect is 20%.
10-20% Better Chance of Getting Magic Items is variable.
Fixed charges: Level 7 Spirit of Barbs (11 charges), Level 5 Heart of Wolverine (13 charges), Level 2 Oak Sage (15 charges).

items.name: Death's Web
items.category: Necromancer wand (elite unique) — roll AND socket dependent
items.quality: Perfect = -50% Enemy Poison Resist, +2 Poison & Bone, plus a socket for a poison Rainbow Facet
items.rarityTier: Very rare drop; socketed + -50 copies scarce
items.priceSignal: Among the highest-demand Necro items — diablo2.io price-check #745 shows a wide spread by roll, and shops sell separate '+1 PnB / 45-49% resist' budget versions vs top '+2 / -50' versions. A socketed copy (holding a poison facet) commands a premium over an identical unsocketed one.
items.collectorCase: Two axes of value on one wand: the -Enemy Poison Resistance roll (-40 to -50) and whether it carries a socket for a poison Rainbow Facet. A -50 socketed Death's Web is a genuinely different item from a -42 unsocketed one, and it is the uncontested BiS for poison Necro with no alternative.
items.whyValuable: -% enemy poison resistance is extremely rare and multiplies poison damage against Hell targets that otherwise resist; plus up to +4 to the key skills. There is no substitute weapon for the build.
items.teachingPoint: Socket count changes a unique's ceiling: Death's Web doesn't drop socketed, so a socket (for -5% enemy poison resist from a facet, plus its poison skill damage) is a value-adder that only some copies have. Quote it as resist roll + socket, e.g. '-50 1-socket'.
items.veteranBlindspot: Players remember the -50 target but forget the socket is a separate, price-moving variable — a socketed -50 is the collector copy, not just any -50.
factClaims: Death's Web is a unique Unearthed Wand (elite), required level 66.
+2 to All Skills is fixed.
+1 to 2 to Poison and Bone Spells (Necromancer only) is variable.
-40 to -50% to Enemy Poison Resistance is variable and is the value stat; perfect is -50.
+7-12 Life after each Kill and +7-12 Mana after each Kill are variable.
It does not drop with a socket; socketed copies (holding a poison Rainbow Facet) trade at a premium over unsocketed.

items.name: Tomb Reaver
items.category: Polearm (elite unique) — ethereal + socket + ED, merc weapon
items.rarityTier: Very rare in the chase configuration (eth AND 3 sockets AND high ED)
items.priceSignal: One of the most sought merc weapons; a 3-socket ethereal with strong ED is a high-rune/High-end trade on diablo2.io and the Blizzard trade forums, well above a 1-socket non-eth copy. Explicitly stocked by shops as a premium eth/3os SKU.
items.collectorCase: The variable stack (ethereal state × 1-3 sockets × 200-280% ED × MF roll) means the top copy is a genuinely rare intersection of four rolls. An eth 3-socket high-ED Tomb Reaver is the museum version; a 1-socket non-eth is a common merc filler.
items.whyValuable: Top magic-find merc weapon: huge ED and undead damage, all-res, life-after-kill, and 50-80% MF, and three sockets to load with Zod (indestructible) + Ist/facets. Ethereal adds 50% damage.
items.teachingPoint: Ethereal is pure upside on merc weapons because mercenary-equipped items never lose durability — no repair, no Zod required. Combine that with a 1-3 socket range and a wide ED range and you get four independent value multipliers on one name.
items.veteranBlindspot: Vets know eth 3os is 'the good one' but under-appreciate how rare the full intersection is — most Tomb Reavers fail on socket count, ethereal, or ED, which is why the complete piece is a trophy.
factClaims: Tomb Reaver is a unique Cryptic Axe (elite polearm).
+200-280% Enhanced Damage is variable.
It spawns with 1 to 3 sockets (variable).
All Resistances +30-50, 50-80% Better Chance of Getting Magic Items, and +10-14 Life after each Kill are variable.
Mercenary-equipped items never lose durability, so an ethereal Tomb Reaver is pure upside for a merc.

items.name: Crown of Ages
items.priceSignal: Consistently high demand; shops maintain distinct SKUs — '2 sockets 15% DR', '2 sockets', '1 socket 15% DR' — which proves the socket count and DR roll set the price. A 2-socket 15DR/30res copy is a high trade; a 1-socket low-res copy is a fraction of it.
items.collectorCase: The classic socket-count value cliff. A 1-socket Crown of Ages and a 2-socket copy are priced worlds apart because the second socket is a whole extra Ber (or facet). Add the DR% and res rolls and the perfect 15/30/2os is the museum helm.
items.whyValuable: Elite defensive helm: +1 skills, base DR%, big resists, indestructible, and up to two sockets. Two Bers reach ~31% total DR from the helm — a survivability piece for PvP and hardcore.
items.teachingPoint: This is the textbook 'socket count changes everything' unique. The DR and res rolls matter, but the 1→2 socket jump alone can double the price. Quote as DR/res/sockets, e.g. '15/30/2os'.
items.veteranBlindspot: Everyone knows 2os is better, but under-rates how sharply value falls off a 1-socket copy — a beautiful 15/30 with one socket still isn't the chase item.
factClaims: Crown of Ages is a unique Corona (elite helm), required level 82, introduced in patch 1.10, and is indestructible.
+50% Enhanced Defense and +100-150 Defense.
+1 to All Skills and 30% Faster Hit Recovery are fixed.
Damage Reduced by 10-15% is variable.
All Resistances +20-30 is variable.
It spawns with 1 to 2 sockets (variable); the second socket is the primary value driver.
Perfect is 15% Damage Reduced / +30 All Resistances / 2 sockets.

items.name: Titan's Revenge
items.quality: Chase = ethereal, high ED (toward +200%); often upgraded to Matriarchal Javelin
items.rarityTier: Ethereal copies notably rarer and premium
items.priceSignal: The defining Javazon weapon; ethereal copies carry a clear premium on diablo2.io and shops (e.g., 'Titan's Revenge Ethereal 150-184% ED' as its own product) over the plentiful non-eth version. Non-eth is affordable; eth high-ED is the sought copy.
items.collectorCase: A rare case where ethereal is desirable on a MAIN character's own weapon, not just a merc's. Because it replenishes its own quantity, an ethereal Titan's gives the full +50% ethereal damage while the javelin stack refills itself — the downside that kills most ethereal weapons is designed away.
items.whyValuable: BiS thrower for Lightning Fury Javazons; +2 amazon + javelin/spear skills, ED, leech, FRW, and a self-refilling stack. Ethereal is 50% more damage.
items.teachingPoint: Ethereal-only value: normally ethereal means it breaks and can't be repaired, so it's a merc-only trait. Replenish Quantity refills the thrown stack, so the eth version is self-sustaining — one of the few ethereal weapons practical for the player, not just the hireling.
items.veteranBlindspot: Some vets reflexively pass on ethereal thrown weapons ('it'll break'); Titan's is the exception where ethereal is strictly better, and that's exactly the kind of counter-intuitive value the item is prized for.
factClaims: Titan's Revenge is a unique Ceremonial Javelin (exceptional), required level 42.
+150-200% Enhanced Damage is variable.
+2 to Amazon Skills and +2 to Javelin and Spear Skills are fixed.
It has Replenishes Quantity [1 in 3 sec] and Increased Stack Size [60].
5-9% Life Stolen per Hit is variable; it also gives +30% FRW, +20 Strength, +20 Dexterity.
It can be upgraded to a Matriarchal Javelin (elite) via Lum + Pul + Perfect Emerald + the item.
Because it replenishes its own quantity, an ethereal copy stays usable on a main character despite ethereal's normal breakage downside.

items.name: Andariel's Visage
items.category: Helm (elite unique) — ethereal merc piece, roll + hidden penalty
items.quality: Chase = ethereal, high ED/str/leech; -30 fire res offset with a socket
items.priceSignal: Best merc helm and a top melee helm; ethereal copies are a distinct premium product on diablo2.io and every shop. Non-eth is common and cheap-ish; eth with good ED/str is the sought copy.
items.collectorCase: Ethereal + high ED + high strength + max leech is a rare stack, and the item hides a trap: a fixed -30% fire resist. The connoisseur copy is an ethereal high-roll that has already solved the penalty with a Ral or fire-res jewel — a considered piece, not a raw drop.
items.whyValuable: +2 skills, 20 IAS, life leech, big strength and defense on a merc = huge survivability and damage. Ethereal adds 50% defense, and merc gear never breaks.
items.teachingPoint: Ethereal-only value again (merc durability is free), but with a lesson in fixed downsides: the -30 fire resist is not a roll — it's always there, and a collector-grade copy is socketed to cancel it. Value = ethereal + ED/str/leech rolls minus how well the penalty is handled.
items.veteranBlindspot: Vets grab 'eth Andy' for the merc and forget the -30 fire res quietly tanks the merc's Hell survivability until it's socketed off — the finished, offset copy is the real collector item.
factClaims: Andariel's Visage is a unique Demonhead (elite helm), required level 83.
+100-150% Enhanced Defense is variable.
+2 to All Skills and 20% Increased Attack Speed are fixed.
8-10% Life Stolen per Hit is variable; +25-30 to Strength is variable.
Fire Resist -30% is a fixed penalty; Poison Resist +70% is fixed.
Ethereal copies are prized because mercenary-equipped items never lose durability; the -30 fire resist is usually offset with a Ral rune or fire-resist jewel in a socket.

items.name: Herald of Zakarum
items.category: Paladin shield (exceptional unique) — ethereal ED roll
items.quality: Perfect ethereal = +200% Enhanced Defense (ethereal adds 50% on top)
items.priceSignal: In demand for Smiter/blocker Paladins; shops list 'Ethereal 200% ED Perfect' as a top SKU distinct from '150-184% ED', confirming the ED roll plus ethereal set the price. A perfect eth is a real trade; a non-eth 150% is budget.
items.collectorCase: The whole premium sits in the ED roll amplified by ethereal — a perfect eth 200% produces an enormous shield defense number that a 150% non-eth can't approach. The +2/+2 skills, 30 ICB, all-res +50 are fixed, so the collector variable is purely ED × ethereal.
items.whyValuable: One of the best Paladin shields: +2 pal + combat skills, big block, all-res +50, strength/vit. The ethereal high-ED copy maximizes the defense wall for Smite ubers and PvP.
items.teachingPoint: On defense-based gear, a % Enhanced Defense roll multiplied by ethereal's +50% defense compounds — the same reason eth armor bases are chased. Quote it as ED + ethereal, e.g. '200 eth'.
items.veteranBlindspot: Once the iconic Hammerdin/Smiter shield and famously duped, many treat any HoZ as interchangeable; the market pays specifically for the perfect ethereal ED, which is a small slice of drops.
factClaims: Herald of Zakarum is a unique Gilded Shield (exceptional Paladin shield), required level 42.
+150-200% Enhanced Defense is variable and is the key roll on an ethereal copy.
+2 to Paladin Skills and +2 to Combat Skills are fixed.
30% Increased Chance of Blocking, 30% Faster Block Rate, +20 Attack Rating, +20 Strength, +20 Vitality, and All Resistances +50 are fixed.
Ethereal adds 50% more defense on top of the Enhanced Defense roll.

items.name: Mara's Kaleidoscope
items.priceSignal: The perfect 30 is one of the most demanded unique amulets — quoted around Lo/Sur (or Sur + a couple Ist) on diablo2.io/d2jsp, distinctly above a 20-res copy which trades for mid runes. Shops sell '30 All Res' as the premium SKU.
items.collectorCase: Included as the canonical proof of the mechanic: one variable stat (all-res 20-30) swings the price from mid-runes to Lo/Sur. The +2 skills and +5 attributes are fixed, so a 30 and a 21 Mara are the same item to a novice and very different to a market.
items.whyValuable: +2 all skills plus universal resistances on the amulet slot — a stat every build wants, and the 30 version is the resist-capping BiS for many setups.
items.teachingPoint: Sometimes the whole price is a single number with a 10-point range. 'Perfect' here is trivially defined (30 res) yet multiplies value several-fold — a clean illustration of roll-driven pricing.
items.veteranBlindspot: This one veterans DO know — flagged honestly. Its value here is as the reference example, not a surprise; still worth cataloguing because it anchors the whole roll-dependence concept.
factClaims: Mara's Kaleidoscope is a unique amulet, required level 67.
+2 to All Skills and +5 to All Attributes are fixed.
All Resistances +20-30 is variable and is the value stat; perfect is 30.
A perfect 30-res copy is among the most valuable unique amulets in D2R.

items.name: Steelrend
items.category: Gloves (elite unique) — ignored ED roll, extreme drop rarity
items.valueTierGuess: C (rare but niche) / B for a perfect on a str-stacking melee build
items.rarityTier: One of the rarer unique glove drops
items.priceSignal: Thin but real: shops bin it by ED band ('30-49% ED' vs '50-59% ED'), so the roll is priced, but overall demand is modest because most melee builds run Dracul's or Laying of Hands. This is a rarity/roll collector piece more than a high-liquidity trade — honest call.
items.collectorCase: A rarity-and-roll piece rather than a money piece. Steelrend gives the highest strength bonus of any gloves (up to +20) and a big +30-60% ED that players ignore because they equip it for the strength alone. The perfect 60/20 is a rarely-seen, rarely-perfect drop — a cabinet item for a collector, with the honest caveat that raw demand is niche.
items.whyValuable: Highest str of any glove plus crushing blow and a real ED roll — a strength-stacking/crushing-blow option for melee that also helps meet other gear's strength requirements.
items.teachingPoint: Another 'value stat hidden behind the reason you equip it': people take Steelrend for +20 str and never read the +30-60% ED, which is the roll that actually varies the item's ceiling.
items.veteranBlindspot: Many veterans have barely seen one drop and think of it purely as a strength glove; the ED roll and the sheer drop rarity are the collector angle, even though it isn't a chase-price item.
factClaims: Steelrend is a unique Ogre Gauntlets (elite gloves), required level 70, required strength 185.
+170-210 Defense is variable.
+30-60% Enhanced Damage is variable and is the value/roll stat; perfect is 60%.
10% Chance of Crushing Blow is fixed.
+15-20 to Strength is variable — the highest strength bonus of any gloves in the game.

items.name: Dracul's Grasp
items.category: Gloves (elite unique) — leech roll + unique proc mechanic
items.quality: Perfect = 10% Life Stolen per Hit / +15 Strength
items.priceSignal: Steady mid-tier demand — trades roughly Mal–Ist range on diablo2.io/forums, with a perfect 10% leech / 15 str commanding the premium end and low rolls sitting cheaper. Not a top-rune item, but liquid and consistently wanted by melee.
items.collectorCase: The only item in the game with 5% Chance to Cast Life Tap on Striking — a mechanic-collector piece by itself — layered on a 7-10% leech roll. The perfect-leech copy is the survivability chase for physical melee, and the unique proc is the reason it never fully goes out of style.
items.whyValuable: Stacks life leech, open wounds, and the Life Tap proc (enemies return 50% of damage as life) — enormous sustain for Zealers, Barbs, and other melee; also +str for gear thresholds.
items.teachingPoint: Value can hinge on a roll (7→10% leech) sitting next to a one-of-a-kind fixed mechanic (Life Tap proc). Traders quote the leech and strength; the proc is why the floor price stays up even on mediocre rolls.
items.veteranBlindspot: Vets know Dracul's for Life Tap and forget the leech is a 7-10 roll that moves price; the perfect 10/15 is the copy worth holding, not any Dracul's.
factClaims: Dracul's Grasp is a unique Vampirebone Gloves (elite), required level 76.
7-10% Life Stolen per Hit is variable and is a key roll; perfect is 10%.
+10-15 to Strength is variable; +90-120% Enhanced Defense is variable; +5-10 Life after each Kill is variable.
25% Chance of Open Wounds is fixed.
5% Chance to Cast Level 10 Life Tap on Striking — the only item in the game with this modifier.

items.name: Arkaine's Valor
items.category: Body armor (elite unique) — HISTORIC: value collapsed when a patch rewrote its ranges
items.quality: Once a 1.08 god-armor; ranges gutted in 1.09/1.10
items.rarityTier: Common drop today; historically a duped chase item
items.priceSignal: Today it trades cheap — outclassed by Enigma/CoH/Fortitude and stocked as a budget armor. Its interest is historical, not current price. This is the collapse case, included for the pillar of patch history rather than live demand.
items.collectorCase: The definitive 'a patch changed the ranges and the value evaporated' story. In 1.08 Arkaine's Valor was one of the strongest, most-duped armors in the game; the 1.09/1.10 rewrite cut its defining stats to a fraction and it never recovered. A veteran who only knows post-1.10 D2 has no idea it was once a god item — that gap is the collector angle.
items.history: In patch 1.08 Arkaine's Valor carried +200% Enhanced Defense, +2.5 Vitality per Character Level, +2 Life per Character Level, +2 to All Skills, 30% Faster Hit Recovery, Indestructible, and 50% Fire Resist — absurd life/vitality scaling that made it a top-tier, heavily duped armor. Patch 1.09 (August 2001, which introduced runewords) began the nerf wave, and by 1.10 it was rewritten to +150-180% Enhanced Defense, +1-2 to All Skills, +0.5 Vitality per Character Level, 30% Faster Hit Recovery, and Damage Reduced by 10-15 — the per-level Life removed and per-level Vitality cut fivefold. The same 1.09 wave hit other 'god' uniques including Harlequin Crest (Shako) and Wizardspike.
items.whyValuable: Historically valuable for its per-level Life and Vitality (a life pool no other armor matched at the time); today valuable mainly as a piece of economic/patch history.
items.teachingPoint: A 'perfect' roll is patch-relative. When Blizzard rewrites a unique's variable ranges, the old chase item can become a vendor drop overnight — the mirror image of D2R's 2.4 buffs, which resurrected dozens of dead uniques. Value tracks the current stat file, not the name.
items.veteranBlindspot: Younger D2R veterans dismiss Arkaine's as a leveling armor and don't know it was once a duped, top-of-the-economy item — the collapse is invisible unless you played 1.07-1.08.
factClaims: Arkaine's Valor is a unique Balrog Skin (elite armor).
In patch 1.08 it had +200% Enhanced Defense, +2.5 Vitality per Character Level, +2 Life per Character Level, +2 to All Skills, 30% Faster Hit Recovery, Indestructible, and 50% Fire Resist.
By patch 1.10 it was +150-180% Enhanced Defense, +1-2 to All Skills, +0.5 Vitality per Character Level, 30% Faster Hit Recovery, and Damage Reduced by 10-15.
The 1.09 patch (August 2001) that introduced the first runewords also nerfed several top uniques including Arkaine's Valor, Harlequin Crest, and Wizardspike.

notes:
Baseline is a mature D2R ladder economy; all "perfect" targets and demand read against that. Every checkable stat (ranges, required levels, socket behavior, patch history) was verified against at least one authoritative DB (diablo2.io, Fandom, d2runewizard, fextralife) plus a trade source; a few points I could NOT fully confirm and left out rather than guess: Verdungo's exact required level (stated only as elite Mithril Coil), and Tomb Reaver's exact required level (stated only as elite Cryptic Axe). diablo2.io blocks the WebFetch tool (HTTP 403), so its numbers came via search snippets and were cross-checked elsewhere.

Sub-topics from the brief, mapped: (1) which single stat traders care about — called out per item (Verdungo DR%; Griffon -Enemy Lightning Resist; Fathom/Nightwing Cold Skill Damage; Wisp Lightning Absorb; Death's Web -Enemy Poison Resist; Mara all-res; Steelrend/Herald/Titan/Tomb ED; Dracul leech). (2) Shorthand — rolled/max notation like Verdungo "15/40", Griffon "-20/15", Fathom "30", CoA "15/30/2os", Mara "30". (3) Why 1% multiplies value — the skill-damage and -enemy-resist rolls are multipliers (Fathom, Griffon, Nightwing), and vendors literally bin those items into 5% price bands. (4) Socket count — Crown of Ages 1→2 (value cliff), Death's Web 0→1 (facet), Tomb Reaver 1-3. (5) Ethereal-only value — Titan's Revenge (self-refilling stack), Tomb Reaver / Andariel's / Herald (merc gear never loses durability), plus the eth-caster note on Death's Fathom. (6) Value collapsed on a patch range change — Arkaine's Valor (1.08 god-armor gutted in 1.09/1.10), with the general lesson that "perfect" is patch-relative.

Deliberately CUT to keep the collector bar high (documented here so the curator sees the filtering): Ravenfrost "20 dex" — the single most famous roll example, but obscurity 1, every veteran already knows it, so it fails the surprise filter; use only as a gateway explainer if needed. Vampire Gaze (15-20% DR / 10-15 MDR roll) — mechanically a fine roll-dependent case, but the item is cheap and a perfect one causes no real value jump, so it fails the price filter. War Traveler (30-50% MF) — same problem, cheap and well-known. 4-socket Crystal Sword and similar trivially-farmed bases — out by definition.

Two accuracy flags for the writer to preserve: Herald of Zakarum's roll is Enhanced DEFENSE (it's a shield), not enhanced damage — easy to mistype. And Andariel's Visage's -30% fire resist is a FIXED penalty, not a roll — the collector copy is one already socketed to offset it.
